name: Salmon with Roasted Vegetables
description: A one-tray dinner: lemon and garlic salmon roasted with sweet potato and broccoli. Minimal washing up.
ingredients: 1 medium sweet potato (about 200 g), cut into 2 cm cubes
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C / 425°F).
Toss the sweet potato with half the oil, the paprika and a pinch of salt on a lined tray. Roast for 15 minutes first; it needs longer than the salmon.
Toss the broccoli with the remaining oil and the garlic and add it to the tray.
Make space in the middle and lay the salmon skin-side down. Season it and top with the lemon slices.
Roast for 12 minutes more, until the salmon just flakes. For moist salmon, take it out at 52-55°C in the centre.
Squeeze over the lemon wedge and scatter with herbs and chilli flakes.
tip: Omega-3 fats, quality protein and slow-release carbs make this an ideal recovery dinner after a key session.

name: Black Bean and Sweet Potato Bowl
description: Roasted cumin sweet potato, garlicky black beans and charred corn with avocado and lime yogurt.
ingredients: 2 medium sweet potatoes (about 400 g), cut into 2 cm cubes
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C / 425°F). Toss the sweet potato with the oil, half the cumin, the paprika and a pinch of salt. Roast for 25-30 minutes, tossing halfway, until soft and caramelised.
Warm the beans in a pan with the garlic, the remaining cumin and a splash of water, lightly crushing a few.
Char the corn in a dry frying pan over a high heat for 3 minutes.
Stir the lime zest, half the juice and a pinch of salt into the yogurt.
Divide everything between two bowls, top with the avocado, lime yogurt and coriander, and squeeze over the rest of the lime.
tip: Very high in fibre. It's a great rest-day dinner, but have something gentler the night before a race.

name: Chicken Parmesan
description: Crisp Parmesan-crumbed chicken escalopes baked under marinara and mozzarella, served over spaghetti.
ingredients: 200 g marinara sauce, plus extra for the pasta
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C / 425°F). Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally into two thin escalopes, or bash it to 1 cm thick, so it cooks fast and stays juicy.
Set out three plates: the flour seasoned with salt and pepper, the beaten egg, and the panko mixed with the Parmesan. Coat each escalope in flour, then egg, then press it firmly into the crumbs.
Heat the oil in an ovenproof frying pan over a medium-high heat and fry the chicken for 2-3 minutes each side until golden.
Spoon the marinara over each piece, top with mozzarella and move the pan to the oven for 8-10 minutes, until the cheese bubbles and the chicken reaches 74°C.
Meanwhile, cook the spaghetti and toss it with a little extra warm marinara.
Serve the chicken on the pasta, scattered with basil.
tip: A big, carb-rich dinner. Save it for after your longest run of the week.

name: Chicken Tikka Masala
description: Yogurt-marinated chicken charred under the grill, then simmered in a spiced tomato and cream sauce. Served with basmati.
ingredients: 600 g chicken breast, cut into 3 cm chunks
steps: Mix the chicken with the yogurt, garam masala, turmeric, chilli powder, salt and lemon juice. Marinate for 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
Heat the grill to high. Spread the chicken on a foil-lined tray and grill for 10-12 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. It finishes cooking in the sauce.
Meanwhile, cook the rice.
For the sauce, heat the oil and butter in a large pan and fry the onion for 8-10 minutes until deep golden. Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the paste for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and 100 ml water and simmer for 10 minutes. Blend until smooth, if you like.
Stir in the cream, then the chicken and any juices. Simmer for 5 minutes, scatter with coriander and serve with the rice.
tip: Lots of protein and carbs for recovery. The curry tastes even better the next day.
storage: The curry keeps for 3 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

name: Beef Tacos
description: Juicy spiced beef in warm corn tortillas with cheddar, crisp lettuce, tomato and soured cream. Homemade taco seasoning, no packet.
steps: Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes.
Turn the heat to high, add the mince and cook for 6-8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the spices, 1/2 tsp salt and the tomato purée for 1 minute, then add 100 ml water and simmer for 5 minutes until saucy.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20-30 seconds each side and stack them in a tea towel to keep soft.
Fill with the beef, cheese, lettuce, tomato, soured cream and salsa, and serve with lime.
tip: Corn tortillas make this gluten-free. For more carbs after a long run, add a side of rice and beans.

name: Shrimp Pad Thai
description: Wok-tossed rice noodles with prawns, egg and bean sprouts in a sweet-sour tamarind sauce, topped with peanuts and lime.
ingredients: 4 spring onions, cut into 3 cm lengths
steps: Soak the noodles in hot (not boiling) water for 8-10 minutes, until pliable but still firm; they finish cooking in the wok. Drain.
Mix the tamarind, fish sauce, sugar and chilli with 2 tbsp water. Taste it: it should be sweet, sour and salty in balance.
Heat the oil in a wok over a very high heat. Stir-fry the garlic and shallot for 30 seconds, then the prawns for 1-2 minutes until pink.
Push everything to one side, crack in the eggs and scramble them for 30 seconds.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss with tongs for 2-3 minutes, until the sauce is absorbed. Add a splash of water if they stick.
Toss in the bean sprouts, spring onions and half the peanuts for 30 seconds. Serve with the remaining peanuts, lime and coriander.
tip: Rice noodles are easy to digest, so this is a good carb-rich dinner the night before a long run.

name: Vegetarian Chili
description: A thick, smoky three-bean chilli with peppers and warm spices, topped with cheddar. Makes enough for the freezer.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion and peppers for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and spices for 1 minute, then the tomato purée for 1 minute more.
Add the tomatoes, beans, stock and sugar. Simmer uncovered for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick.
Season, add a squeeze of lime, and top with the cheddar.
tip: Serve it over rice or a baked potato to turn it into a proper training-day dinner.
storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

name: Lamb Chops with Mint
description: Rosemary and garlic lamb chops seared pink, with minty crushed new potatoes and peas.
steps: Rub the chops with half the oil, the garlic, rosemary, lemon zest, salt and pepper. Leave them at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes, adding the peas for the last 3. Drain, then roughly crush them with a fork, the remaining oil and the chopped mint.
Heat a griddle pan until very hot. Stand the chops on their fat edge for 2 minutes to render and crisp it.
Cook for 3 minutes each side for pink (about 60°C). Rest for 5 minutes.
Serve with the crushed potatoes and mint sauce.
tip: Lamb is rich in iron and B12, both important for runners, especially women in heavy training.

name: Chicken Enchiladas
description: Corn tortillas rolled around chicken and black beans, baked in a smoky chipotle tomato sauce under melted cheddar.
steps: Put the chicken in a pan, cover with water, bring to a gentle simmer and poach for 12-15 minutes until cooked. Rest, then shred. Leftover cooked chicken works too.
For the sauce, simmer the passata with the chipotle, 1 tsp of the cumin, the oregano and a pinch of salt for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil and cook the onion and pepper for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, paprika and remaining cumin for 1 minute, then stir in the beans, chicken and 4 tbsp of the sauce.
Heat the oven to 190°C fan (210°C / 410°F). Wrap the tortillas in damp kitchen paper and microwave for 30 seconds; cold corn tortillas crack when you roll them.
Fill and roll each tortilla, then lay them seam-side down in a baking dish. Pour over the remaining sauce and scatter with cheese.
Bake for 20 minutes until bubbling. Serve with soured cream, coriander and lime.
tip: Assemble them the day before and bake after your run. Dinner's ready in 20 minutes.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge; also freezes well, unbaked.

name: Moussaka
description: A lighter moussaka: roasted aubergine and potato layered with cinnamon-spiced lamb under a golden Greek yogurt topping.
ingredients: 300 g potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C / 425°F). Brush the aubergine slices with the oil, season, and roast on two trays for 20-25 minutes until soft and golden. Roasting instead of frying saves a lot of oil. Meanwhile, parboil the potato slices for 5 minutes and drain.
Brown the lamb in a dry pan over a high heat for 6-8 minutes and pour off excess fat. Add the onion for 5 minutes, then the garlic, cinnamon and oregano for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato purée and tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until thick. Season.
Whisk the yogurt, egg, half the Parmesan and the nutmeg.
In a baking dish, layer the potatoes, half the aubergine, the lamb sauce and the rest of the aubergine. Spread the yogurt topping over and scatter with the remaining Parmesan.
Turn the oven down to 180°C fan and bake for 35-40 minutes until golden and set. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting; it slices cleanly once it settles.
tip: A weekend cook that gives you four dinners. Pair it with crusty bread for extra carbs.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer, in portions.

name: Paella
description: Saffron rice with chicken, prawns, mussels and peas, cooked in one wide pan until a crisp crust forms underneath.
ingredients: 400 g boneless, skinless chicken thighs, in chunks
steps: Put the saffron in the hot stock and keep it warm. Scrub the mussels and pull off the beards; throw away any that are open and don't close when tapped.

Heat the oil in a paella pan or wide frying pan and brown the chicken for 6-8 minutes. Push it aside, soften the onion and pepper for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and paprika for 1 minute and the tomatoes for 3 minutes.
Stir in the rice to coat it, then pour in the hot stock with a good pinch of salt. Stir once to spread everything evenly, then don't stir again; that's how the crust (socarrat) forms.

Simmer on a medium heat for 10 minutes. Press the prawns and mussels (hinge down) into the rice and scatter over the peas. Cook for 8-10 minutes more, until the rice has absorbed the liquid, the mussels have opened and the prawns are pink.
Turn up the heat for the last minute and listen for crackling: that's the crust.
Take it off the heat, cover with a tea towel for 5 minutes, and throw away any mussels that haven't opened. Serve with lemon and parsley.
tip: A carb-rich celebration meal. It fits the night before a long run or the evening after a race.

name: Ratatouille
description: Provençal vegetable stew with aubergine, courgette, peppers and tomato, plus butter beans to make it a meal. Better the next day.
steps: Cut all the vegetables to the same size so they cook evenly.
Heat 1.5 tbsp of the oil in a large pan over a high heat. Fry the aubergine for 5-6 minutes until golden, then lift it out. Cooking it separately lets it brown instead of steam.
Fry the courgettes in the same pan for 4 minutes and lift them out.
Add the remaining oil and cook the onion and peppers for 6-8 minutes. Add the garlic and herbs for 1 minute.
Add the tomato purée, tomatoes, beans and the reserved vegetables. Simmer, partly covered, on a low heat for 25-30 minutes until tender but still holding their shape.
Season and tear in the basil.
tip: Serve with crusty bread, quinoa or polenta; on its own it's light on carbs for a training day.
storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge; the flavour improves overnight.

name: Eggplant Parmesan
description: Baked, not fried: roasted aubergine layered with garlicky tomato sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan under a crisp crumb.
ingredients: Pinch each of salt and sugar
50 g Parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, grated
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C / 425°F). Brush the aubergine slices with most of the oil and roast for 20-25 minutes until soft and golden.
Meanwhile, simmer the passata with the garlic, salt, sugar and a few basil leaves for 10 minutes.
In a baking dish, layer sauce, aubergine, mozzarella and a little Parmesan three times.
Mix the panko with the remaining Parmesan and oil and scatter it over the top.
Turn the oven down to 180°C fan and bake for 25-30 minutes until bubbling and golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.
tip: Serve with pasta or garlic bread to make it a proper training-day dinner.

name: Baked Ziti
description: Pasta tubes in a beefy tomato sauce with pockets of ricotta, baked under bubbling mozzarella. Family-size comfort food.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C / 425°F). Cook the pasta for 3 minutes less than the packet says; it finishes in the oven.
Meanwhile, heat the oil and brown the mince with the onion for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and oregano for 1 minute, then the passata, and simmer for 10 minutes. Season.
Season the ricotta with half the Parmesan and some pepper.
Mix the drained pasta into the sauce. Spoon half into a baking dish, dot with the ricotta, then add the rest of the pasta.
Top with the mozzarella and the remaining Parmesan and bake for 20-25 minutes until bubbling and browned. Scatter with basil.
tip: Plenty of carbs and protein. Leftovers reheat well for a post-run lunch.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge or 2 months in the freezer.

name: Korean Bibimbap with Beef
description: Rice topped with marinated beef, seasoned vegetables and a fried egg, stirred together with a sweet-spicy gochujang sauce.
steps: Cook the rice. Freeze the beef for 15 minutes, slice it thinly, and marinate it in the soy sauce, half the sesame oil, the sugar and garlic for 15 minutes.

Cook the vegetables separately, each seasoned with a pinch of salt: stir-fry the carrot, then the courgette, in a little vegetable oil for 1-2 minutes each. Blanch the spinach and bean sprouts in boiling water for 30-60 seconds, squeeze them dry and toss with the remaining sesame oil.
Stir-fry the beef in a very hot pan for 2-3 minutes until browned.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up.
Mix the gochujang, honey, vinegar and 1 tbsp water to make the sauce.
Arrange the rice in bowls with the vegetables and beef in sections and the egg on top. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and stir everything together with the sauce before eating.
tip: A generous carb and protein refuel. Make it the evening after a long or hard run.

name: Korean Kimchi Stew
description: Kimchi jjigae: a bubbling, spicy stew of well-fermented kimchi, pork and silken-soft tofu, served with rice.
ingredients: 100 g short-grain rice, cooked, to serve
steps: Heat the sesame oil in a pot over a medium heat and cook the pork for 4-5 minutes until browned at the edges.
Add the garlic and kimchi and fry for 3-4 minutes. Frying the kimchi deepens the flavour; older, sourer kimchi works best.
Stir in the gochugaru and gochujang for 30 seconds.
Add the water or stock, kimchi juice and fish sauce. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the tofu and courgette and simmer for 8 minutes more.
Scatter with spring onions and serve bubbling, with the rice.
tip: Spicy and salty. Great on a cold evening, but not the night before a race.

name: Cod with Garlic and Herbs
description: Flaky cod under a lemon, garlic and parsley crust, roasted on a tray of new potatoes, courgette and tomatoes.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C / 425°F). Toss the potatoes with 1 tbsp of the oil and some salt and roast for 15 minutes.
Add the carrot, courgette, onion and tomatoes to the tray and roast for 10 minutes more.
Mix the garlic, parsley, lemon zest, oregano and the remaining oil.
Nestle the cod among the vegetables, season it, and spread the herb mixture over the top.
Roast for 10-12 minutes, until the cod is opaque and flakes easily. Squeeze over the lemon juice.
tip: Lean protein with moderate carbs. It's light, so it's a good choice the evening before a morning session.

name: Mediterranean Chicken Roast
description: Oregano and lemon chicken thighs roasted over peppers, courgettes, tomatoes and chickpeas, finished with olives and feta.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C / 425°F).
On a large tray, toss the vegetables and chickpeas with 1.5 tbsp of the oil, half the oregano, the garlic and some salt.
Season the chicken with the remaining oil and oregano, the lemon zest, the paprika, salt and pepper, and lay it on top of the vegetables.
Roast for 30-35 minutes, until the chicken reaches 74°C and the vegetables are charred at the edges.
For the last 5 minutes, scatter over the olives and feta. Squeeze over the lemon juice to serve.
tip: Serve it with crusty bread or couscous to soak up the juices and add carbs.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Chicken and Vegetable Curry Stew
description: A gently spiced turmeric and coconut stew of chicken, sweet potato and carrot, finished with spinach and lime.
ingredients: 600 g chicken breast, cut into chunks
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over a medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 5 minutes. Lift it out.
Soften the onion for 6-8 minutes, then add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the spices and tomato purée and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and stock, add the sweet potato and carrots, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Return the chicken and simmer for 10 minutes, until the potato is tender and the chicken cooked through. Meanwhile, cook the rice.
Stir in the spinach and lime juice, season, and serve with the rice and coriander.
tip: Turmeric and ginger give it an anti-inflammatory edge, and it's gentle enough for a hard training week.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

name: Braised Chicken with Root Vegetables
description: Crisp-skinned chicken thighs braised in white wine and thyme with carrots, parsnips and new potatoes. One pot, big flavour.
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C fan (180°C / 350°F). Season the thighs well.
Heat the oil in a casserole over a medium-high heat. Brown the chicken skin-side down for 6-8 minutes, until deep golden and crisp, then flip it for 2 minutes and lift it out.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp of the fat. Soften the onion for 5 minutes, then add the carrots, parsnips, garlic and thyme for 3 minutes, and the tomato purée for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and bubble for 2 minutes, scraping up the browned bits. Add the stock, bay leaves and potatoes.
Return the chicken skin-side up, with the skin above the liquid so it stays crisp. Cover and cook in the oven for 45 minutes, then uncover for 15 minutes until tender and reduced.
Rest for 5 minutes and scatter with parsley.
tip: Hands-off Sunday cooking that covers two post-run dinners in the week.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Honey Garlic Glazed Salmon
description: Salmon baked and then grilled under a sticky honey, garlic and ginger glaze, with rice and green vegetables.
ingredients: 250 g green beans or tenderstem broccoli
steps: Cook the rice. Whisk the honey, soy sauce, garlic, ginger and vinegar together to make the glaze.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C / 425°F). Line a tray with foil, because the honey burns and sticks. Lay the salmon on it skin-side down, brush with oil and spoon over half the glaze.
Bake for 10-12 minutes.
Meanwhile, simmer the remaining glaze in a small pan for 1-2 minutes until syrupy. Steam the greens for 4 minutes.
Switch the grill to high, spoon the thickened glaze over the salmon and grill for 1-2 minutes, watching closely, until caramelised.
Serve with the rice and greens.
tip: Omega-3s plus fast carbs. It's a strong choice the evening after a key workout.

name: Pork Tenderloin with Apple Cider Glaze
description: Juicy roast pork tenderloin with buttery apples in a sticky cider, maple and mustard glaze, served with mash.
ingredients: 200 ml dry cider or unsweetened apple juice
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C / 425°F). Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until tender.
Season the pork. Heat the oil in an ovenproof pan and sear it on all sides for 5-6 minutes.
Roast for 12-15 minutes, to 63°C (just pink), then rest it under foil for 8 minutes. Tenderloin is lean and dries out fast above 65°C.
Put the same pan on the hob. Melt the butter and fry the apple slices for 3-4 minutes until golden, then add the shallot for 1 minute.
Add the cider, maple syrup, mustard and thyme and bubble for 4-5 minutes until syrupy. Stir in the pork's resting juices.
Mash the potatoes with the milk and season. Slice the pork and spoon over the glaze and apples.
tip: Pork tenderloin is one of the leanest proteins around, which makes this a light but satisfying recovery dinner.

name: Indian Butter Chicken
description: Tender marinated chicken in a silky, gently spiced tomato and butter sauce (murgh makhani), served with basmati.
ingredients: 600 g boneless, skinless chicken thighs, in chunks
steps: Marinate the chicken in the yogurt, half the garam masala, the chilli powder, lemon juice and 1 tsp salt for at least 20 minutes.
Sear the chicken in a hot pan for 5-6 minutes until browned, then lift it out. Cook the rice.
Melt the butter in the same pan and cook the onion for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, paprika, cinnamon and the remaining garam masala for 1 minute.
Add the passata and sugar and simmer for 10 minutes, then blend until smooth.
Stir in the cream and chicken and simmer for 10 minutes until cooked through. Crumble in the fenugreek, if using, and serve with the rice.
tip: Milder than tikka masala, so it's a crowd-pleaser, with a solid protein and carb refuel.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

name: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemons
description: Chicken thighs slow-simmered with ras el hanout, saffron, preserved lemon and green olives, served over fluffy couscous.
ingredients: 2 tsp ras el hanout (or 1 tsp each cumin, ground ginger and paprika, plus 1/2 tsp each cinnamon and turmeric)
Pinch of saffron in 400 ml hot chicken stock
steps: Toss the chicken with the spices and a pinch of salt. Heat the oil in a tagine or heavy casserole and brown the chicken for 5 minutes, then lift it out.
Cook the onions for 8-10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the saffron stock and honey, return the chicken, cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes.
Add the preserved lemon and olives and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes to thicken. Taste before adding salt; the lemons are salty.
Put the couscous in a bowl, pour over 250 ml boiling water or stock with a pinch of salt, cover for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Serve the tagine over the couscous, scattered with herbs.
tip: The salty sauce is welcome after hot-weather training.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

name: Mushroom Risotto
description: Creamy arborio rice with golden mushrooms, white wine, thyme and Parmesan, stirred until it flows like lava.
ingredients: 40 g Parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, grated
steps: Keep the stock at a simmer in a separate pan; cold stock stalls the rice.
Heat the oil and half the butter in a wide pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft.
Turn up the heat, add the mushrooms and cook for 6-8 minutes until golden and their liquid has gone. Salt them only once they've browned. Add the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the edges look translucent. Pour in the wine and stir until it's absorbed.
Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring often and waiting until each ladleful is mostly absorbed. After 18-20 minutes the rice should be creamy and just tender, with a slight bite.
Take it off the heat, beat in the remaining butter and the cheese, cover for 2 minutes, then season and scatter with parsley.
tip: Rice-based comfort food with lots of carbs and little fibre. It makes a good pre-long-run dinner.

name: Grilled Pork Tenderloin
description: Dijon and cider-vinegar marinated pork tenderloin with charred griddled vegetables and new potatoes.
ingredients: 1 pork tenderloin (about 500 g), silver skin trimmed
1 tsp olive oil, for the vegetables
steps: Whisk the oil, vinegar, mustard, honey, garlic, rosemary, salt and pepper. Set 1 tbsp aside to dress the finished dish (never reuse marinade that has touched raw meat).
Coat the pork in the rest and marinate it in the fridge for 30 minutes to 4 hours.
Boil the potatoes for 12 minutes, drain and halve them.
Heat a griddle or barbecue to high. Cook the pork for 12-15 minutes, turning every 3 minutes, to 63°C in the centre. Rest for 8 minutes.
Toss the vegetables and potatoes with the oil and griddle them for 3-4 minutes each side.
Slice the pork and drizzle it with the reserved dressing.
tip: Lean and high in protein. It's a good summer dinner on the barbecue after an evening run.

name: Coconut Curry with Tofu
description: Crisp golden tofu and vegetables in a fragrant Thai red curry and coconut sauce with lime and basil, over jasmine rice.
ingredients: 2 tbsp vegan Thai red curry paste (many contain shrimp paste, so check the label)
300 g mixed vegetables (broccoli, pepper, green beans)
steps: Press the tofu between kitchen paper under something heavy for 10 minutes, then cut it into cubes. Start the rice.
Heat half the oil in a large pan and fry the tofu for 8 minutes, turning, until golden on several sides. Lift it out.
Add the remaining oil and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the curry paste for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and stock, add the vegetables (the hardest ones first) and simmer for 6-8 minutes.
Return the tofu and add the soy sauce, sugar and lime juice. Scatter with basil and serve with the rice.
tip: A plant-based recovery dinner with a good carb load. Make it milder with less paste if spice upsets your stomach.

name: Lemon Herb Grilled Chicken
description: Chicken marinated in lemon, garlic, parsley and thyme, griddled until juicy, with rosemary roast potatoes and salad.
ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil, plus 3 tbsp for the marinade
steps: Mix 3 tbsp oil with the lemon juice, parsley, thyme, garlic, salt and pepper. Flatten the chicken to an even thickness and marinate it for 30 minutes to 4 hours. Any longer and the lemon turns the texture mushy.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C / 425°F). Toss the potatoes with 1 tbsp oil, the rosemary and salt, and roast for 35 minutes.
Heat a griddle over a medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 5-6 minutes each side, to 74°C.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes, then slice. Serve with the potatoes and salad.
tip: Grill all four breasts and use the leftovers for lunches: salads, wraps and pasta boxes.

name: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
description: Silky, tender beef and crisp broccoli in a glossy garlic, ginger and oyster sauce, over jasmine rice. Faster than a takeaway.
ingredients: 450 g beef sirloin, thinly sliced against the grain
1 tbsp soy sauce, plus 1 tbsp for the sauce
1 tbsp cornflour, plus 1 tsp for the sauce
steps: Toss the beef with 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp cornflour, the bicarbonate of soda and 1 tsp of the oil. Leave it for 15 minutes; this velveting keeps it tender. Start the rice.
Mix the oyster sauce, remaining soy sauce, sugar, 1 tsp cornflour and 100 ml water.
Blanch the broccoli in boiling water for 1 minute and drain. It stays tender without steaming the wok.
Heat a wok until smoking and add 1 tbsp of oil. Lay the beef in a single layer and leave it for 1 minute, then flip and cook for 1 minute more. Lift it out.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the garlic and ginger for 20 seconds, then the broccoli and pepper for 2 minutes.
Add the sauce and beef and toss for 1 minute until glossy. Drizzle with the sesame oil and serve over the rice.
tip: Iron-rich beef with plenty of carbs. Batch the sliced, marinated beef in the freezer for quick midweek dinners.

name: Filipino Adobo with Chicken
description: Chicken braised in soy, vinegar, garlic and bay, then browned and glazed in the reduced sauce. The Philippines' national dish.
ingredients: 1 head of garlic, cloves peeled and crushed
steps: Combine the chicken, soy sauce, garlic, bay leaves and peppercorns in a pan. Marinate for 30 minutes if you have time.
Add the vinegar and 120 ml water and bring to the boil. Don't stir for the first 5 minutes; this lets the vinegar's sharpness cook off.
Cover and simmer for 25 minutes. Meanwhile, cook the rice.
Lift out the chicken and pat it dry. Fry it in the oil in a separate pan for 3-4 minutes each side until browned.
Meanwhile, boil the sauce hard with the sugar for 5 minutes until syrupy. Return the chicken and turn it to coat. Serve with the rice.
tip: High in sodium, which is handy after a hot, sweaty session. Go easy on the sauce otherwise. Even better the next day.
storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

name: Bacalhau à Brás
description: A Portuguese favourite: flaked cod, soft onions and crisp matchstick potatoes bound with barely set eggs, finished with olives and parsley.
ingredients: 250 g salt cod, soaked (or fresh cod)
steps: If you're using salt cod, soak it in cold water in the fridge for 24-48 hours, changing the water 3-4 times. Poach it for 5 minutes, then flake it, removing the skin and bones. For fresh cod, season it with salt and poach for 5 minutes.

Heat the oven to 220°C fan (240°C / 465°F). Cut the potatoes into very thin matchsticks (a julienne peeler or mandoline helps). Rinse and dry them thoroughly in a tea towel, toss with 1 tbsp oil and salt, and spread thinly over two lined trays. Bake for 15-20 minutes, tossing halfway, until golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, cook the onion slowly in the remaining oil for 10 minutes until soft and sweet. Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the cod, and warm it through for 2 minutes.
Beat the eggs with pepper. If you used salt cod, don't add salt.
Turn the heat to low, add the potatoes to the pan, pour in the eggs and stir gently for 1-2 minutes, until just creamy. They should be soft, not dry.
Take it off the heat and finish with the parsley and olives.
tip: Essentially an egg-and-potato scramble: easy protein and carbs that go down well after a long run.

name: Turkey and Lentil Bolognese
description: A lighter ragu of turkey mince and red lentils in tomato, over spaghetti. Lentils add fibre and iron, and nobody notices they're there.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and soften the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes.
Turn up the heat, add the turkey and cook for 6 minutes until browned.
Stir in the garlic, oregano and tomato purée for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, tomatoes and stock. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally and adding water if it gets thick, until the lentils melt into the sauce. Season.
Meanwhile, cook the spaghetti. Toss it with the sauce and a splash of the pasta water, and serve with the Parmesan.
tip: High-carb and high-protein, with more fibre than a classic bolognese. A dependable weeknight refuel.
storage: The sauce keeps for 3 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

name: Carb-Load Tomato and Basil Pasta
description: A simple, low-fibre, low-fat pasta in a garlicky tomato sauce, built for the days before a long race.
ingredients: Pinch each of salt and sugar
steps: Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water.
Meanwhile, warm the oil in a small pan and cook the garlic gently for 1 minute, without letting it colour.
Add the passata with the salt and sugar and simmer for 8 minutes.
Drain the pasta, keeping a splash of the water, and toss it in the sauce with that water.
Tear over the basil and finish with the Parmesan.
tip: For the 36-48 hours before a long race: lots of carbohydrate, not much fat or fibre, nothing spicy. Scale the pasta up to your needs. A full carb-load is roughly 8-10 g of carbs per kg of body weight per day, spread across several meals. Try it before a long training run first.

name: Chicken and Chorizo Rice
description: A one-pan Spanish-style rice with smoky chorizo, chicken thighs, peppers and peas. Portugal's arroz de frango meets paella.
ingredients: 70 g cooking chorizo, diced (check it's gluten-free if needed)
500 g boneless, skinless chicken thighs, in chunks
steps: Fry the chorizo in the oil in a wide, lidded pan for 3 minutes until it releases its red oil.
Add the chicken and brown it for 5 minutes.
Add the onion and pepper for 5 minutes, then the garlic and paprika for 1 minute.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute to coat it, then add the tomatoes, hot stock and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on a low heat for 15 minutes.
Scatter over the peas, cover again, and cook for 5 minutes more until the rice is tender.
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve with parsley and lemon.
tip: Carb-rich and easy to batch. It makes a good dinner two nights before a long race.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Reheat until piping hot.

name: Red Lentil Dal with Spinach
description: Silky turmeric and ginger red lentils finished with a sizzling cumin, mustard seed and tomato tarka, served with basmati.
steps: Rinse the lentils until the water runs clearer. Simmer them with the water, turmeric and ginger for 20-25 minutes, skimming off any foam and stirring occasionally, until they collapse.
Meanwhile, cook the rice.
For the tarka, heat the oil in a frying pan and add the cumin and mustard seeds. When they pop (about 30 seconds), add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, chilli and garam masala for 1 minute, then the tomatoes for 3 minutes.
Stir the tarka and spinach into the dal. Add the lemon juice and season with salt.
Serve over the rice with coriander.
tip: Cheap, plant-based and carb-rich. Lentils are a good iron source for vegan runners; eat them with vitamin C, like the tomato and lemon here.
storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.

name: Sheet-Pan Chicken Fajitas
description: Smoky spiced chicken, peppers and onions roasted on one tray, wrapped in warm tortillas with avocado, salsa and yogurt.
ingredients: 500 g chicken breast, cut into strips
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C fan (240°C / 465°F).

On a large tray, toss the chicken, peppers and onion with the oil, spices, lime zest and 1/2 tsp salt. Spread them in one layer; use two trays if it's crowded, because packed vegetables steam instead of charring.
Roast for 20 minutes, stirring halfway, until the chicken is cooked and the peppers are charred at the edges.
Wrap the tortillas in foil and warm them in the oven for the last 5 minutes.
Squeeze the lime juice over the tray and serve with the tortillas, avocado, yogurt, salsa and coriander.
tip: Twenty minutes, one tray, and more than 50 g of protein per serving.

name: Teriyaki Tofu Rice Bowl
description: Crispy cornflour-coated tofu in a sticky homemade teriyaki sauce, over jasmine rice with broccoli and carrot.
ingredients: 1 tbsp cornflour, plus 1 tsp for the sauce
steps: Press the tofu for 10 minutes, cut it into cubes, and toss with 1 tbsp cornflour and a pinch of salt.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice and cook it with 225 ml water: bring to the boil, cover and cook on a low heat for 12 minutes, then rest for 5.
Fry the tofu in the oil over a medium-high heat for 8-10 minutes, turning, until crisp all over.
Steam the broccoli and carrot for 4 minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, maple syrup, vinegar, ginger, garlic, 1 tsp cornflour and 3 tbsp water. Pour it over the tofu in the pan and bubble for 1-2 minutes until thick and glossy.
Serve over the rice with the vegetables, sesame seeds and spring onions.
tip: A vegan recovery bowl with a big carb load. Leftover tofu is good cold in a lunch box.

name: Sausage and Bean Casserole
description: Browned sausages simmered with two kinds of beans, peppers and smoked paprika in a rich tomato sauce. Proper winter comfort.
steps: Heat the oil in a casserole over a medium heat and brown the sausages for 8-10 minutes until golden all over; they finish cooking in the sauce. Lift them out and halve them.
Cook the onion, carrots and pepper for 6-8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, paprika, thyme and tomato purée for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans, stock and Worcestershire sauce, then return the sausages.
Simmer covered for 20 minutes, then uncovered for 10 minutes until thick. Season.
tip: Serve with mash, a baked potato or crusty bread to make it a full training-day dinner.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer.
